message.content:
In lions, the most well‑documented **dominant** genetic trait is the presence of a mane.  
The allele that codes for a mane is dominant over the allele that produces a maneless phenotype. In other words, if a lion inherits one copy of the mane allele (from either parent), it will develop a mane; only when it inherits two copies of the recessive “maneless” allele does it remain without a mane. This dominance pattern is why male lions almost always have a mane, while females (who are homozygous recessive for this trait) do not.
